newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Anite set to return to the black.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Anite set to return to the black.

text.p: Anite Group Plc is set to return to the black in the current financial year following its transformation into a slimmed-down systems and networks support company.
"We're profitable now," said chairman Alec Daly in a telephone interview. "In the first two months of the year the company overall is in the black."
While he could not give a forecast for the year, Daly stressed the group would show a pre-tax profit this year.
Earlier, Anite reported a pre-tax loss of 50.4 million stg for the year to April 30, compared with a loss of 19.2 million stg the year before.

The principle reason for the widening loss was a charge of 32.2 million stg -- 21.9 million of which was taken at the half year -- to meet liabilities arising from its surplus properties following a detailed review.
"We've taken professional advice on the long-term effect of that and we've provided for it, which we think is realistic and prudent so as we can now get the company off to a clean start".
The figures also incorporate the disposal of the group's data communications manufacturing activities announced at the half year.
These disposals helped wiped out the company's debt -- it now has a net cash balance of 15.5 million stg compared with debts of 29.6 million at the end of last year.
The disposals have "transformed Anite", leaving it with just two businesses, systems and networks, which are both cash-generating, growth areas, said Daly.
"We're very positive about those two divisions in terms of their potential," he said.
Daly said no further disposals were anticipated as the group now focuses on its two divisions.
"We've got all the bad news out on the table and from here on in we're hoping, and planning, for much better things," he added.
Trading in the current financial year has been satisfactory.
Daly said he could not at this stage give a dividend forecast. It gave no dividend this year or last.
